Themes

The palettes the demos can draw in: what a theme is, the radius layers, and a page for each palette.

One look, more than one palette

A theme is one AppTheme: the TypeScript spec defineTheme() compiles — tokens, metrics, elevation, eleven surfaces, feedback, motion and controls — and the theme.json that same build exports from it (the roles of both appearances, three radius-* layer lengths and the fixed scrim / media / on-media values). A theme that ships beside another is a sparse delta over it, so it states only what it changes. An app is built with one theme and can carry more, switching between them while it runs with selectTheme.

Each built-in theme distills the visual style of its design system — colors, radii, surfaces, and motion — rather than replicating every platform widget 1:1. Apple, Material, and WinUI record that mapping under Design notes and trade-offs. A theme of your own is Customizing.

Every demo on this site can be drawn in any of these palettes: pick one with the Demo theme switch in the nav, and the previews load again in it. The panel above is the showcase — buttons, a card with a field, badges, switches, a slider and a progress bar, with the card, inset and press surfaces the palette brings. The list is apps/website/demos/palettes.ts. Each palette has its own page, with the same sections: how to install it, every token it sets, and every surface it draws. Those pages read each theme's own spec. The contract is docs/theme.md.

Radii by role

theme.json states one corner radius per layer in cssVars.theme — radius-md (in-page elements), radius-lg (cards, menus, popovers, toasts) and radius-xl (dialogs, sheets) — and control("button").corner.* makes buttons capsules (material, touch apple) or points / control (the rest). A surface nested in another takes the concentric corner, rounded(outer, inset). Every corner that reads a theme radius uses shape.curve ("continuous" or "circular"), which rounded() applies in one place.
